title: Arthur Lawrence's 12:38 PM Fishersville Sweep, VITA's 120-Day Unsigned Form, & The 5:00 PM Resignations
subtitle: What Happened in Fishersville After Katie and Nate Caught the Bus Back to Staunton—and Why Cross and Saunders Resigned Before 5:00 PM
location: Bates-Harding Building & Barton Hall, Roosevelt Rehabilitation Center, Fishersville, Virginia
recipient: Readers of Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 11, Chapter 5, Part 1)
relatedBookLabel: Episode 11, Chapter 5: Street Clothes on the Route 250 Connector & Calling the Governor
summary: Behind-the-scenes chronicle of Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence, State Inspector General Kenneth Dalton, VITA CIO Rajiv Patel, and Acting DARS Commissioner Angela Thornton arriving in Fishersville at 12:38 PM—uncovering VITA's 120-day unsigned VLAN form, lobby video of Greg Saunders, and two more 5:00 PM resignations.
html:
Archival Note: At 9:48 AM on Thursday, July 22, 2027 in Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 11, Chapter 5, U.S. Senator Katie Prairie and Nathaniel Prairie slide their visitor badges back under the glass at the Bates-Harding Building, sign out, catch the westbound SVT Route 250 Connector into downtown Staunton for lunch on Beverley Street, and ride eastbound ARTS Train 50 back to Alexandria. Meanwhile, while Governor Rebecca Langford was securing DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling's resignation on Capitol Square, Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence was already speeding westbound up Interstate 64 toward Fishersville. Here is what happened inside Roosevelt Rehabilitation Center between 9:49 AM and 8:15 PM.

1. Three Frozen Hours in Fishersville & The Bombshell VITA CIO Rajiv Patel Found on I-64 West (9:49 AM – 12:38 PM)

For sixty seconds after the automatic glass entrance doors slid shut behind Katie and Nate's SwiftChair power wheelchairs at 9:49 AM, nobody in the Bates-Harding front visitor lobby breathed.

  1. Why Nobody Dared Touch a Single Yellow Pass Before 1:00 PM:
    Breaking the silence, Assistant Director Greg Saunders stepped nervously toward the interior reception door and asked in a hushed voice whether housekeeping should box up the four-inch stack of canary-yellow Level 2 pass pads and the October 2019 handbooks from the lobby rack before the Richmond cars arrived.
    Ashen-faced, Director Evelyn Cross stopped him instantly:
    • Not only had Arthur Lawrence warned them live on speakerphone that "we already have Nate's inventory list" (meaning Nate Prairie had already logged timestamped counts and form numbers into his laptop),
    • Under Va. Code § 2.2-311, concealing, altering, or removing state records after an inspection by the Office of the State Inspector General (OSIG) has been announced converts an administrative disaster into a criminal misdemeanor obstruction charge. For the next two hours and forty-nine minutes, the canary-yellow pass stack sat untouched behind the glass like an unexploded bomb.
  2. The 11:12 AM Discovery Near Charlottesville (Cross Left VITA's Approval Unsigned for 120 Days!):
    Meanwhile, climbing toward Afton Mountain in the lead state SUV alongside Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence, State Inspector General Kenneth Dalton, and newly appointed Acting DARS Commissioner Angela Thornton (followed by a second agency van carrying two OSIG forensic auditors and three senior VITA network engineers), VITA Chief Information Officer Rajiv Patel opened his encrypted tablet to pull up the "pending quarterly security board exception ticket" that Dr. Cross had blamed in front of Senator Prairie for keeping all twelve Web & Software Applications classroom desktops locked down.
    Halfway past Charlottesville at 11:12 AM, Patel stared at his screen and let out an audible groan of disbelief:
    • RRC's local coordinator had submitted Ticket #INC-2027-44109 on Friday, March 19, 2027—one month after the Senate Appropriations hearing.
    • Four days later—on Tuesday, March 24, 2027 at 10:18 AM—VITA's Enterprise Network Engineering team had APPROVED the isolated classroom developer VLAN, attaching a standard one-page Facility Director Classroom Network Acknowledgment Form for Dr. Evelyn Cross (with a copy to Greg Saunders) so VITA could push unlocked local web-server, PHP, and database images overnight!
    • Automated VITA reminder pings had gone to Cross and Saunders on April 7, May 5, June 2, and July 7, 2027. Neither Cross nor Saunders had ever signed the one-page form—leaving twelve state-funded workstations dark for 120 straight days while telling disabled students, instructors, Richmond, and the United States Senate that "VITA's security board" was holding them up!

2. 12:38 PM — Walking Through the Front Lobby Doors Twenty-Two Minutes Ahead of Schedule

At 12:38 PM—twenty-two minutes ahead of Arthur Lawrence's 1:00 PM promise—two dark Commonwealth SUVs pulled to the curb outside the Bates-Harding Building, forty feet from the Roosevelt Avenue bus stop sign where Katie and Nate had rolled off that morning.

Walking briskly through the exact same aluminum-framed front entrance doors, Arthur Lawrence, Inspector General Kenneth Dalton, VITA CIO Rajiv Patel, and Acting DARS Commissioner Angela Thornton stepped straight up to the glass visitor sign-in window, signed their names directly underneath Katie and Nate's 9:48 AM sign-out lines, and fanned out across campus:

  1. OSIG Seizes the Lobby Rack & Uncovers June Purchase Order #27-0894 (5,000 Fresh Yellow Passes):
    Inspector General Dalton's auditors photographed and bagged the front-desk stack of canary-yellow Barton Hall Level 2 Off-Campus Hall Passes, the laminated 11:00 PM adult-sibling lockout notice, and the Revised October 2019 handbooks. Worse still for RRC management, a ten-minute check of Fishersville's procurement ledger turned up Purchase Order #27-0894 (dated June 18, 2027)—personally approved by Assistant Director Greg Saunders four months after the February 17 Senate hearing—ordering 5,000 freshly printed sheets of canary-yellow Level 2 passes from the state print shop!
  2. Pulling the July 15 Lobby Camera Video (Catching Greg Saunders Red-Handed):
    Working directly from Nate's morning audit notes (Kayla's bus account that an intake supervisor in the front lobby had grabbed her friend Marcus's wheelchair push-handles without consent the previous Thursday and threatened an aggression write-up), OSIG investigators pulled the Bates-Harding front-lobby security camera archive for Thursday, July 15, 2027 (1:14 PM) and spoke privately with twenty-year-old Marcus in Barton Hall.
    On high-definition lobby video, the administrator who walked behind Marcus's manual wheelchair at the intake counter, yanked his rear push-handles backward without asking, and wagged a finger in Marcus's face threatening a disciplinary behavioral note when Marcus objected was Assistant Director Greg Saunders himself.
  3. Instructors Hand Over Cross's May 3 Slides—And VITA Unlocks All Twelve Lab Workstations Before 4:15 PM:
    Inside the Web and Software Applications classroom, the relieved lead instructor—who had spent five months begging administration to unlock his room—handed OSIG auditors a printed copy of Dr. Cross's May 3, 2027 Division Heads Quantum Presenter slide deck, which instructed faculty in black and white to "maintain existing 2019 intake and residential handbook workflows pending completion of the July 29 Senate Appropriations markup."
    Standing right beside the twelve dark, VITA-tagged desktop towers, VITA CIO Rajiv Patel pulled the unsigned March 24 Classroom VLAN Form up on his tablet in front of a mortified Dr. Cross, handed the stylus to Acting Commissioner Angela Thornton—who signed it on the spot in fifteen seconds—and turned his three network engineers loose. By 4:15 PM that same afternoon, VITA had provisioned a dedicated, hardware-isolated gigabit instructional VLAN and imaged unlocked developer accounts (PHP, local web servers, relational databases, and Quantum Code) across all twelve dual-monitor desktop workstations—allowing Trevor (the honors web-design graduate from Katie and Nate's 8:30 AM bus ride) and his seven classmates to unplug the daisy-chained orange floor surge strips before the end of class!
  4. Dumping the Waynesboro ValueMart Greeter Flyers & Suspending Yellow Passes on the Spot:
    Two doors down in the Vocational Evaluation suite, Acting Commissioner Thornton swept the entire wire tray of Waynesboro ValueMart Retail Greeter Readiness flyers straight into a recycling bin, signed an immediate directive exempting Trevor and every college-degreed or credentialed student from manual-shop Voc Eval rotations effective that hour, and walked over to Barton Hall—with zero RRC managers allowed inside—to tell Kayla, Marcus, and twenty-nine fellow residents face-to-face that canary-yellow Level 2 passes and adult family lockout rules were abolished effective immediately.

3. 3:40 PM – 4:25 PM — Who Resigned, Why They Left, & The Legal Difference Between Being Fired vs. Resigning

Why did three officials (DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling in Richmond, plus RRC Director Dr. Evelyn Cross and Assistant Director Greg Saunders in Fishersville) all submit signed resignations before 5:00 PM on Thursday, July 22, 2027—and why did the Governor demand resignations rather than simply saying "You're fired"?

The Legal & Career Difference Between Being Fired vs. Demanded Resignation in Virginia Government

In executive state governance, "have your resignation on my desk before five o'clock" is not a polite favor—it is a razor-sharp legal and administrative lever that differs dramatically from an involuntary firing:

  1. At-Pleasure Appointees (Va. Code § 2.2-106) vs. Agency Employees (Virginia Personnel Act & DHRM Policy 1.60):
    • Commissioner Marcus Sterling was a direct gubernatorial appointee serving "at the pleasure of the Governor" (Va. Code § 2.2-106 & § 51.5-131), meaning Governor Langford could fire him unilaterally at 5:00 PM with zero appeal rights—and Sterling resigned at 10:22 AM solely to avoid having a public Executive Order of Removal for Cause (citing his June 14 email and false statements to Congress) permanently destroy his ability to sit on any board or hold any job in his field.
    • Director Dr. Evelyn Cross and Assistant Director Greg Saunders, by contrast, were agency-appointed DARS administrators governed by the Virginia Personnel Act (Va. Code § 2.2-2900) and *Department of Human Resource Management (DHRM) Policy 1.60 (Standards of Conduct). Firing a state facility employee involuntarily for a Group III Offense (Falsification of Official State/Federal Records) legally requires issuing a formal Written Pre-Disciplinary Due-Process Notice, placing them on suspension during a mandatory 24-to-48-hour employee response window, and opening the door to months of administrative hearings under the Virginia State Grievance Procedure (Va. Code § 2.2-3000)*.
    • What a Signed Resignation Accomplishes Instantly: The second an agency administrator signs a resignation letter effective 5:00 PM, 100% of their statutory due-process waiting periods, grievance appeals, and litigation hooks vanish permanently—allowing Acting Commissioner Angela Thornton to install an interim facility leadership team at 5:01 PM the exact same day without six months of personnel hearings!
  2. Why Cross and Saunders Signed Instead of Fighting (The Group III Guillotine):
    Sitting across the Bates-Harding conference table from Arthur Lawrence, State Inspector General Dalton, and Acting Commissioner Thornton between 3:40 PM and 4:25 PM, neither Cross nor Saunders resigned "out of politeness." They signed because forcing the Commonwealth to fire them carried catastrophic lifelong consequences:
    • Dr. Evelyn Cross (Signed at 3:48 PM): Cross had co-signed Line 2 of the false congressional compliance report, authored the May 3 "wait until the July 29 markup" faculty slide deck, and sat on VITA's March 24 classroom VLAN approval for 120 days while blaming VITA to a United States Senator. Had she refused to resign, Acting Commissioner Thornton had a Group III Suspension-Pending-Termination Notice ready on the table—which would permanently stamp "Terminated for Cause — Falsification of Official Federal Compliance Report (Ineligible for Commonwealth Rehire)" across every state agency and public university database in Virginia, forfeit transition privileges, and trigger a mandatory misconduct referral to her doctoral rehabilitation-administration licensing board. At 3:48 PM, Cross signed a three-sentence resignation effective 5:00 PM, packed one cardboard box alongside the cold travel mug of coffee she had walked through the front doors with at 9:00 AM, and drove out of the staff lot at 4:12 PM.
    • Assistant Director Greg Saunders (Signed in Lieu of Group III Termination at 4:20 PM): Confronted ten minutes later with (a) his co-signature on the internal Fishersville attestation worksheet, (b) June's Purchase Order #27-0894 for 5,000 newly printed canary-yellow passes, and (c) the July 15 front-lobby security video catching him grabbing twenty-year-old Marcus's wheelchair push-handles without consent and threatening a retaliatory aggression write-up, Saunders learned that OSIG's formal investigative report would name him personally for both record falsification and retaliation against a disabled resident if a Group III termination hearing went forward. At 4:20 PM, Saunders signed his resignation in lieu of termination effective 5:00 PM and surrendered his master keycard at the front security podium.

4. 8:15 PM — The Same-Night Audit Readout Sent to Dirksen Room 511

Just as eastbound ARTS Train 50 delivered Katie and Nate back to Alexandria (ALX) and the twins rolled through David's front door on Sunset Drive for dinner, Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence and State Inspector General Kenneth Dalton transmitted their promised written readout from Fishersville to Dirksen Room 511:

Encrypted CPI Administrative Mail Dispatch VERIFIED ARCHIVE

MEMORANDUM — OFFICIAL AUDIT READOUT
To: The Honorable Katie Prairie, United States Senate (Dirksen Room 511)
From: Arthur Lawrence, Chief of Staff to Governor Rebecca Langford; Kenneth Dalton, State Inspector General (OSIG)
Cc: Dr. Miriam Alcott, Secretary of Health and Human Resources; Angela Thornton, Acting Commissioner (DARS); Rajiv Patel, Chief Information Officer (VITA)
Date: Thursday, July 22, 2027, 8:15 PM EDT
Subject: Same-Day Fishersville On-Site Findings, 5:00 PM Executive Resignations, & Emergency Directive Implementation

1. Resignations Accepted Effective 5:00 PM Today (July 22, 2027): Following independent verification that every item logged by your office at 8:52 AM – 9:48 AM was accurate—and discovery of internal June 14 correspondence intentionally delaying campus reforms until after your Subcommittee's July 29 markup—Governor Langford and Acting DARS Commissioner Angela Thornton demanded and accepted the immediate resignations of DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling (10:22 AM), RRC Director Dr. Evelyn Cross (3:48 PM), and RRC Assistant Director Greg Saunders (4:20 PM).

2. Immediate Campus Actions Completed Today (12:38 PM – 6:00 PM): VITA uncovered an approved March 24 classroom VLAN authorization left unsigned by prior RRC management for 120 days; VITA engineers unlocked all twelve Web & Software Applications developer workstations onto an isolated instructional fiber network by 4:15 PM today. All canary-yellow Level 2 passes, October 2019 handbooks, adult family lockout notices, and retail-greeter Voc Eval flyers have been permanently removed from service, and college-degreed/credentialed clients have been exempted from manual-shop intake rotations effective immediately ahead of Governor Langford's formal 12:00 PM Friday Emergency Executive Directive.

3. Respecting Your Appropriations Hold Standard: Neither the Governor's Office nor DARS requests release of your \$18.5 million Subcommittee hold in next Thursday's markup. OSIG and DARS will return only after independent state and federal RSA unannounced audits—and confidential Barton Hall resident interviews—confirm sustained daily operation when nobody expects an inspection.
